articles.headline: Drought Pre-Alert Spreads Across Galicia's Miño, Sil and Cabe Basins
articles.subtitle: After five months of rainfall running 49 percent below average, the Xunta declared a scarcity pre-alert across the eastern basins, hitting more than 150 concellos as reservoir levels and river flow keep falling
articles.body:
Galicia has moved a step closer to drought. The regional government declared a water-scarcity pre-alert across the whole eastern part of the community, covering the Miño Alto, Cabe, Sil Inferior, Baixo Miño and Limia basins, an area that touches more than 150 concellos. The declaration follows five months in which rainfall was 49 percent below the March-to-July average in the Miño-Sil territory.

According to the latest hydrological bulletin from Spain's Ecology Transition Ministry, reservoirs in the Miño-Sil basin lost 57 cubic hectometres in the past week and sit at 70.4 percent of capacity, while the Galicia Costa basin fell 12 hectometres to 62.1 percent. Drinking-water reserves are healthier, at 80 and 86 percent respectively. River flow is a sharper concern: in the eastern half of the community, circulating flow is 45 percent below its usual July level.

The new alert joins one declared on 8 July across part of the Galicia Costa basin, where the Lérez and part of the Anllóns rivers are causing worry, adding a further thirty municipalities to the pre-alert list. Groundwater reserves are mostly in good shape, though the Xinzo de Limia aquifer and the Louro alluvial plain near O Porriño are strained by habitual over-exploitation. Local spring-fed village water systems are already feeling the lack of rain.

articles.headline: Trailer With Possible Narco-Boat Found Stranded in the Miño River
articles.subtitle: Portuguese maritime police found a semi-rigid high-speed boat valued at over 400,000 euros hidden inside a Spanish-registered trailer partially submerged in the river at Caminha, with no one at the scene
articles.body:
Portuguese maritime and judicial police are investigating a striking find on the Miño river at the port of Lanhelas, in the municipality of Caminha, on the border with Spain. A Spanish-registered trailer was found partially submerged in the river, with a semi-rigid high-speed boat hidden inside it. The authorities were alerted around nine in the morning Spanish time after residents spotted the trailer stopped on the access ramp to the river.

When the first officers arrived they found neither the driver nor anyone nearby. Inspection of the trailer revealed a pneumatic semi-rigid vessel more than twelve metres long, fitted with three high-output engines and carried on a metal structure. Portugal's National Maritime Authority valued the boat at more than 400,000 euros and said the trailer and semi-trailer, of a type frequently associated with logistics used by drug-trafficking networks, were partially submerged and were seized.

The harbour captain of Caminha, Fernando Vieira Pereira, said the initial reconstruction suggests the trailer was in the middle of launching the boat or pulling it out of the water when something went wrong and the vehicle was abandoned. He cautioned that although the vessel matches the pattern of boats used by trafficking organisations, the investigation has only just begun and no link to drug trafficking has been established.

articles.headline: Candia Promises to Pay Lugo Suppliers, Blames Outgoing Government
articles.subtitle: The mayor defended her decision to approve payment of Arde Lucus invoices and said 2.7 million euros owed to 542 suppliers involves old bills from 2023-2025 that never followed proper procedure, accusing PP's rivals of bad faith
articles.body:
Lugo mayor Elena Candia has responded to opposition demands that she unblock payment of 2.7 million euros owed to 542 suppliers, defending her decision to authorise payment of the Arde Lucus invoices by decree and blaming the previous administration for the backlog. In a press conference on Tuesday, Candia said the first question should be why the outgoing government never paid those bills.

She said her team found a large number of unpaid invoices when it took office, and that not all of them are in the same situation. The Arde Lucus 2026 invoices, she argued, were contracted through the proper procedure with budget provision, whereas the 2.7 million euros concerns bills from 2023, 2024 and 2025 that did not follow adequate procedure and in many cases had no budget allocation at all.

She said the Partido Socialista and Bloque Nacionalista Galego had contracted those suppliers and organised those activities without paying for them, and that the current government asked them for clarification before deciding on the invoices. When the matter was brought to the plenary, Candia said, the two groups voted against paying, which she described as an irresponsible position.

She stressed that suppliers should know the previous parties voted no, and committed the government to finding a satisfactory solution despite that opposition.

articles.headline: Prosecutor Seeks 26 Years for Alleged Samos Murder of Octogenarian
articles.subtitle: José Manuel Vázquez Lebón is accused of killing his 82-year-old neighbour with at least twenty knife wounds in Lamas on 4 August 2023 and then stabbing his 75-year-old wife, who survived after a neighbour intervened
articles.body:
The public prosecutor has asked for a 26-year prison sentence for José Manuel Vázquez Lebón, a 52-year-old resident of Samos accused of murdering his neighbour and attempting to kill that neighbour's wife. The crimes took place three years ago on 4 August 2023 in Lamas, in the parish of San Mamede do Couto, and the accused has been in prison since the events.

According to the prosecution, Vázquez had a poor relationship with the victims, who lived only metres from his house. Knowing his 82-year-old neighbour, Manuel López Vázquez, usually left around 8am to tend livestock, the accused is said to have waited by a woodshed intending to attack him by surprise.

He allegedly struck the octogenarian on the head with a log or similar object and, taking advantage of his greater size and strength against the victim's advanced age, attacked him with a knife while shouting threats. The victim suffered at least twenty stab wounds, mostly to the neck, one of which severed the left external jugular vein and another the left common carotid artery.

The man's 75-year-old wife, Consuelo Ánguez, heard the screams and came to help, striking the attacker with a cattle stick, but could not stop him. The accused is said to have then chased and stabbed her repeatedly in the neck. A young neighbour who heard her cries intervened, hitting the attacker with a stick until he stopped and retreated to his home. Ánguez was flown to the HULA hospital, where she spent 13 days in intensive care.

articles.headline: Freight Train Derailment and Bus Collision Disrupt Lugo's O Ceao
articles.subtitle: Within five hours on Tuesday morning, a Captrain goods train left the rails at the industrial park's terminal and a car collided with a town bus on Avenida da Coruña, causing long traffic queues, though nobody was hurt
articles.body:
Lugo's O Ceao industrial park had a busy morning on Tuesday, with a freight-train derailment first thing and a collision between a car and a town bus around midday, barely five hours apart and without any injuries. The derailment happened at the goods terminal of the business park shortly after eight in the morning, when a Captrain train was carrying out manoeuvres off the main line.

Four wagons of the train running the Tui-Lugo goods route left the rails as it stopped at the buffer stop at the end of the line. The wagons did not overturn, but restoring normal operation took several hours, though goods movement continued as planned. Hours later, around two in the afternoon, a car ran into a town bus just before the junction of Avenida da Coruña with the road into the industrial park.

Because the street is narrow and has a single lane at that point, the collision produced significant traffic hold-ups on a road that is particularly busy at those hours. No one was hurt, but a medical team attended to check on the drivers, and both Local Police and the Guardia Civil's traffic division were called.

The car, damaged on its front-right wheel side, ended up turned across Avenida da Coruña, forcing drivers joining the queue to edge onto the pavement briefly to pass. Once the car was removed, traffic resumed normally.

articles.headline: EU Unveils Five-Point Plan to Prevent Another Border Breach Like Ceuta
articles.subtitle: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told Pedro Sánchez in a letter that more must be done to strengthen the EU's external borders, offering enhanced early-warning systems and more technical and financial support to Morocco
articles.body:
The European Union has set out a five-point plan to avoid another mass border breach like the one that saw tens of thousands of migrants surge into Ceuta, as the Commission pressed Spain to strengthen its external border. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez in a letter dated 3 August, seen by Reuters, saying more must be done to strengthen the EU's borders at critical points.

In cooperation with Spain, especially on anything related to Ceuta and Melilla, she offered to enhance border-management early-warning systems and improve technical and financial support to Morocco. The EU commissioner for internal affairs said 75 people died during the mass breach, in which more than 70,000 crossed the border in hours.

The plan follows tensions inside the bloc in which Italy suspended Schengen free travel with Spain for August, France reinforced its border controls with aircraft and hundreds of extra police, and 22 member states called for broader action. Sánchez has criticised what he called a selfish response from some EU governments. The Commission has stressed its support for Spain while insisting that lessons must be learned and gaps closed.

Brussels also expressed backing for the harder-line approach associated with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, a sign of how the Ceuta crisis has shifted the EU's migration debate toward stricter border enforcement.

articles.headline: Trump Support Emboldens Morocco's Ambitions Over Ceuta and Melilla
articles.subtitle: Nearly a week after the migration crisis, La Voz de Galicia reports that Rabat is hinting it could use the situation to push its claim to the two Spanish autonomous cities, encouraged by backing from Washington
articles.body:
Almost a week after the grave migration crisis in Ceuta, the causes remain shrouded in mystery, and Morocco is now hinting it could use the situation to press its claim to the Spanish autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla, according to La Voz de Galicia. The newspaper reports that Rabat is emboldened by support from the United States, and specifically Donald Trump, in advancing its aspirations over the two North African enclaves.

Morocco has long maintained a claim to the territories, which Spain regards as integral parts of its national territory. The crisis began in late July when tens of thousands of migrants surged over the border or swam around the Tarajal breakwater, overwhelming Ceuta's reception facilities and costing at least 67 lives. Spain has argued the episode was orchestrated or exploited by trafficking networks, while some analysts have suggested foreign actors encouraged the pressure.

The reporting notes that Morocco's ambassador had said the situation unfolded against the government's wishes, but that the political climate now sees Rabat testing how far it can press its territorial claims under current circumstances. The Spanish government has rejected Ceuta's request to declare a national emergency, arguing migration does not fall within the legal framework for such declarations, and instead announced additional police deployments and closer coordination with Moroccan authorities.

articles.headline: Ceuta Still Not Normal as 5,000 Migrants Remain and 70,000 Return
articles.subtitle: Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said 70,000 of the 72,000 people who entered the enclave have gone back to Morocco, but the city's president says it has not returned to normal with migrants still on the streets
articles.body:
Four days after the mass influx into Ceuta, the Spanish enclave is still far from returning to normal, with up to 5,000 migrants remaining in the city. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said on Tuesday that 70,000 of an estimated 72,000 people who entered have returned to Morocco. The government has maintained that the immediate crisis has been largely reversed, with the border restored to calm and the majority of those who crossed having gone back.

However, the president of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, has said the city has not returned to normal, with many migrants still on the streets and residents expressing concern about the ongoing situation. The death toll from the crossing has been revised upward, with the EU's internal affairs commissioner citing 75 deaths, while earlier official figures put the number at 67.

The events have triggered a Europe-wide political row, with Italy suspending Schengen travel with Spain for August, France reinforcing border controls, and an emergency meeting of EU interior ministers. The crisis has also revived debate about Spain's migration policy, including its recent regularisation drive, with some European governments arguing such measures incentivise trafficking.

Spain's government has rejected the criticism, insisting it has one of the least porous external borders in the EU and blaming criminal networks for exploiting the situation.

articles.headline: Global Stock Sell-Off: Japan's Nikkei Posts Worst Day Since 1987
articles.subtitle: A shock US jobs report triggered recession fears that sent Tokyo's Nikkei down 12.4 percent, its biggest one-day rout since Black Monday, wiping out more than a quarter of its value from a record high a month earlier
articles.body:
Global markets were hit by a sharp sell-off on Monday as fears of a US recession gripped investors, with Japan's Nikkei 225 index closing down 12.4 percent, its worst single-day performance since the 1987 Black Monday crash. The rout, which began with a weaker-than-expected US jobs report on Friday that pushed unemployment to its highest level in nearly three years, spread across Asia and Europe.

Tokyo's Nikkei lost 4,451 points to close at 31,458, and heavy trading houses such as Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Sumitomo and Marubeni plunged more than 14 percent, with Mitsui losing almost a fifth of its market value. The index is now a quarter below its record high of a month ago. South Korea's Kospi fell sharply and markets in Australia, Hong Kong and China also dropped, while European shares followed Wall Street lower.

A strengthening yen, which hit its strongest level against the dollar since January, added pressure on Japan's export-heavy companies. The sell-off has fuelled debate about whether the US Federal Reserve should have cut interest rates sooner, and has hit major technology stocks, with Apple, Nvidia and Tesla among names down sharply.

Analysts compared the volatility to the 1987 crash, the 2008 financial crisis and the onset of the 2020 pandemic, though some cautioned that the situation differs from those episodes.

articles.headline: US Revokes Brazilian Ambassador's Visa in Escalating Diplomatic Feud
articles.subtitle: The State Department revoked Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti's visa in retaliation for Brazil withholding approval of Trump's ambassador nominee and denying visas to two US diplomats, deepening a clash ahead of October elections
articles.body:
The United States has revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador to Washington, Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti, in a sharp escalation of a diplomatic feud between the Trump administration and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. A senior State Department official said the move was a reciprocal measure after Brazil withheld formal approval of President Trump's nominee to be US ambassador in Brasília, former Florida House speaker Daniel Perez, and denied visas to two American diplomats.

Brazil had earlier refused visas to two US State Department officials, including Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour Riley Barnes, accusing them of attempting to interfere in the country's October presidential election by questioning the integrity of its voting system. The State Department rejected those allegations as baseless, saying the planned visit was a routine engagement. The official said Viotti's visa would be reinstated immediately if Brazil grants diplomatic approval for Perez.

Lula's government has accused the Trump administration of seeking to tilt the election against him, while Washington says it rejects any effort by foreign countries to interfere in its own processes. The dispute has raised concern about the relationship between the two largest economies of the Americas, and comes as Brazil has also downgraded diplomatic ties with Argentina after insults by Javier Milei towards Lula.

articles.headline: Conflicting Signals on Iran as Trump Insists Talks Are Underway
articles.subtitle: Trump claimed negotiations with Tehran would resume Monday after calling off a planned strike, but Iran said it has no plans for direct talks, only narrower discussions with Oman over a single corridor through the Strait of Hormuz
articles.body:
Donald Trump said negotiations with Iran would resume on Monday, a day after he announced he had called off a planned massive strike against the country, but Tehran's leaders gave conflicting signals about whether any such talks are taking place. Trump said on Truth Social that he had agreed to cancel the attack contingent on being able to rapidly make a deal, and later insisted talks were ongoing.

Iran's foreign ministry, however, said Tehran has no plans for direct negotiations with Washington, and is only engaged in talks with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz. Those discussions have focused on agreeing a single corridor for ships to transit, rather than the divided northern and southern routes currently in use.

The proposal Trump announced over the weekend, according to the Associated Press, calls for the US and Iran to return to negotiations, reopening the Hormuz Strait and halting attacks across the region, including by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq. The disparate messages between Washington and Tehran have added to confusion about the status of peace talks and of the war itself, which is entering its sixth month.

Trump has warned Iran it faces a last chance to sign a deal, while Iran's foreign minister has been holding calls with Saudi and Pakistani leaders. The war, which began with major joint US-Israeli strikes on 28 February, has drawn in multiple countries across the region.

articles.headline: More Than 150 Migrants Rescued After Boat Catches Fire in the Channel
articles.subtitle: French authorities said a vessel's engine caught fire while attempting to cross to the UK, prompting a rescue operation that brought more than 150 people to safety as migrant crossings continue amid the English Channel
articles.body:
More than 150 migrants were rescued after a boat caught fire in the English Channel while attempting to cross to the United Kingdom, French authorities said. The vessel's engine caught fire in the middle of the crossing, according to French officials, and rescue teams were dispatched to bring those on board to safety.

The incident is the latest in a continued series of Channel crossings, which have persisted despite ongoing efforts by both the French and British authorities to deter them. The rescue adds to a summer in which migration has dominated political debate across Europe, though the recent Ceuta crisis on Spain's North African coast has drawn much of the attention.

France has been reinforcing its border controls and coastal patrols in response to both Channel crossings and the wider migration pressures facing the continent. The number of people attempting the dangerous crossing has fluctuated through the year, influenced by weather, enforcement and the political climate. French authorities regularly carry out rescue operations for boats in distress, and the English Channel remains one of the busiest and most hazardous migration routes in Europe.

The fate of those rescued was not immediately detailed, but such operations typically see migrants brought ashore and processed by French authorities.

articles.headline: Palantir Soars on Blowout Quarter as US Commercial Revenue Jumps 149%
articles.subtitle: Revenue surged 93 percent to $1.94 billion and adjusted earnings beat estimates, with US commercial business more than doubling, prompting the AI software firm to raise full-year guidance and sending its stock up sharply
articles.body:
Palantir Technologies delivered a blockbuster second-quarter earnings report on Monday, sending its shares up sharply as US commercial revenue nearly doubled and the company raised its full-year outlook. Total revenue surged 93 percent year-over-year to $1.94 billion, comfortably beating the $1.80 billion analysts had expected. Adjusted earnings came in at 41 cents per share, above the 35 cents forecast.

US commercial revenue jumped 149 percent to $764 million, and the company said that on a compounding basis that figure has risen 380 percent since 2024. US government revenue grew 90 percent to $809 million. Chief executive Alex Karp described the quarter as a demonstration of the company's focus on creating real enterprise value, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to 82 percent growth, with US commercial revenue now expected to exceed $3.42 billion.

The company reported GAAP net income of $1.06 billion and more than $1.2 billion in free cash flow. Analysts called it the best quarter in Palantir's history, driven by accelerating enterprise adoption of its AI platforms. The stock has nonetheless lost 29 percent this year, reflecting broader concerns about AI valuations, and Monday's blowout results provide a counterpoint to fears that AI spending may be cooling.

articles.headline: Apple Launches New Legal Challenge Over UK Demand for Encrypted Data
articles.subtitle: The company filed a complaint at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal after the Home Office made a fresh request for a backdoor into British users' encrypted iCloud data, a demand it previously abandoned a year ago
articles.body:
Apple has launched a new legal challenge against a UK government demand to access its customers' encrypted iCloud data, a year after the Home Office agreed to abandon its previous request for global access. The company filed a complaint last month at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that investigates claims that UK intelligence services have acted unlawfully, according to the Financial Times.

The Home Office has made a fresh request for a so-called backdoor into encrypted iCloud data belonging to British users, under an order issued by the court. The UK's Investigatory Powers Act compels companies to provide information to law enforcement agencies working on cases including terrorism and child sexual abuse, and can force firms to give British security services access to customer data even when it is protected by strong encryption.

Apple's earlier legal challenge related to a demand for access to the encrypted data of users worldwide, which sparked tensions between London and Washington and ultimately prompted the UK to drop that request. The current demand is understood to be narrower, focusing on British users, but Apple argues it still undermines the security of its encrypted services.

The case is the latest in a long-running dispute between technology companies and governments over encryption, with Apple maintaining that building backdoors into its products would weaken security for all users.

articles.headline: Engineers Bring DeepSeek V4 Flash to Life on a Single AMD MI300X
articles.subtitle: A detailed write-up chronicles the months of software work needed to run the frontier model on AMD's 2023-vintage accelerator, highlighting the ongoing software gap between AMD and Nvidia hardware
articles.body:
A detailed engineering post has chronicled the long road to running DeepSeek V4 Flash on a single AMD MI300X, a feat that highlights the persistent software gap between AMD and Nvidia hardware in the AI accelerator market. The post, by Fergus Finn, documents that as of early May 2026 running vLLM with DeepSeek V4 Flash on the MI300X simply did not work, and that the problems were almost entirely software rather than hardware.

AMD's MI300X, launched in December 2023 as the company's response to Nvidia's H100, carries 192GB of HBM3 memory per card and remains a large and capable part, but support for running the latest models on it has lagged. The piece notes that while there are signs the gap is closing on AMD's newer chips such as the MI350X and MI355X, that renewed software focus has not always extended back to older parts.

The project required workarounds involving vLLM forks and ROCm fallbacks, with some support for the DeepSeek V4 Flash variant still in open pull requests. The effort has drawn attention on Hacker News, where it sits alongside lively debate about the value of frontier open-weight models and whether they can be run affordably on non-Nvidia hardware.

The wider context is a GPU market where Nvidia parts are scarce and expensive, with on-demand capacity sold out and rental prices climbing, making AMD alternatives increasingly attractive despite the software friction.

articles.headline: Alibaba Unveils Qwen3.8-Max, Its Largest and Most Capable AI Model
articles.subtitle: The 2.4-trillion-parameter multimodal model, which will be open-sourced next week, handles text, images and video and processes up to a million tokens, approaching the size of Moonshot's rival Kimi K3
articles.body:
Alibaba has unveiled Qwen3.8-Max, which it calls its largest and most capable artificial-intelligence model to date, intensifying the race among Chinese AI companies to build ever more powerful systems. The model boasts 2.4 trillion parameters, placing it among the largest open-weight models in the world and not far behind the offering from domestic rival Moonshot AI launched last month.

Parameters are the numerical settings that shape how an AI processes information, and while the count is a shorthand rather than a full measure of capability, a larger model can typically store more knowledge. Qwen3.8-Max will be fully open-sourced next week, continuing the pattern in which Chinese labs publish open weights while the largest US labs mostly keep frontier models closed.

The multimodal foundation model supports visual intelligence and delivers what the company describes as a comprehensive upgrade across coding, real-world work, research and long-horizon tasks. Like Moonshot's Kimi K3, it can handle text, images and video and process up to 1 million tokens at a time, enough to take in long legal files, large software codebases or hundreds of pages of documents.

The release sent Alibaba's shares higher and comes as the company bets on AI and cloud as its main growth driver. It also highlights a broader price war, with research firm Artificial Analysis noting that DeepSeek's latest model offers pricing more than a hundred times cheaper than Anthropic's premium offering.

articles.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI Among AI Firms Facing New EU Enforcement Powers
articles.subtitle: As the AI Act's transparency rules take effect, the EU AI Office now holds supervisory and fining authority over general-purpose models, with penalties up to 15 million euros or 3 percent of global turnover
articles.body:
Anthropic, OpenAI and other developers of general-purpose AI models are now facing new enforcement powers in the European Union, as the bloc's landmark AI Act reaches a major milestone. The transparency obligations under Article 50 have come into full effect, requiring providers and deployers of AI systems to label AI-generated content and disclose when users are interacting with a chatbot.

The EU AI Office now holds supervisory and fining authority over general-purpose AI model providers, with penalties of up to 15 million euros or 3 percent of global annual turnover. The rules apply to any organisation that provides or deploys AI systems within the EU, regardless of where the company is based, meaning US firms such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google face compliance duties across the bloc.

Under the new obligations, providers of generative systems must ensure AI-generated content is identifiable through machine-readable markings, deployers must label deepfakes and AI-generated text published to inform the public, and chatbots must disclose they are AI systems unless this is obvious from context. The European Commission has published guidelines on the transparency obligations. The high-risk AI obligations have been deferred to December 2027 under the Digital Omnibus, but the transparency rules proceed on schedule.

The enforcement marks the first binding transparency regime for AI at this scale anywhere in the world, and companies are now adapting their products and disclosures to comply.
